I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation and only a smaller share in cotton. I am 65, I have farmed for 40 years, some family labor is off-farm, and I have only 8 mu, so I will put stability first. In Quzhou County, the wheat-maize system matches the local climate and water pattern well: winter wheat needs more irrigation, while summer maize uses the summer rain better. Because I have well irrigation, I will protect wheat first, then hold maize steady, and keep cotton on a smaller area for cash income without letting it take too much labor. For inputs, I will stay near current official nutrient ranges for south Hebei and the Huang-Huai-Hai region, then make my own conservative choices inside those ranges rather than pushing for the highest input level. My area split is my own decision; the nutrient ranges and local cropping context are based on official and research sources for Quzhou / Hebei wheat-maize and Huang-Huai-Hai cotton: [Quzhou wheat-maize context](https://www.nature.com/articles/srep41587), [Hebei winter wheat irrigation note, 2026-03-09](https://www.agri.cn/zx/xxlb/hb/202603/t20260309_8817365.htm), [winter wheat fertilization guidance](https://www.agri.cn/sc/nszd/202309/t20230928_8125583.htm), [summer maize fertilization guidance](https://www.moa.gov.cn/govpublic/ZZYGLS/201006/t20100606_1534673.htm), [cotton fertilization guidance](https://www.moa.gov.cn/govpublic/ZZYGLS/202303/t20230314_6423045.htm). The pesticide counts, tillage choices, expected yields, and land allocation are my own inferences from those conditions.
